history.cultural: As with all KÃ¶nigrufen variants, Graden is part of Austria's rich tarock tradition. The game is played in social and family settings, with specific regional clubs maintaining the variant.

setup.players: Four players. Partnerships determined by calling a king or playing solo contracts.
setup.deck: 54-card Austrian Tarock pack: 22 trumps (Tarocks I-XXI plus SkÃ¼s), 8 cards each in four suits (Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds).
setup.dealing: Standard KÃ¶nigrufen deal: 12 cards to each player, 6 cards to talon, dealt in packets of 6 anticlockwise. Play proceeds anticlockwise.

rules.objective: In positive contracts, take at least 36 of 70 card points. Negative contracts have specific objectives like winning no tricks or exact trick counts.
rules.gameplay: Bidding follows the graduated (Graden) structure. Players bid contracts in ascending order of value. After winning bid, declarer may call a king for partner, exchange with talon, and make announcements. Must follow suit, play tarock if void, highest tarock wins.
keyRules: 54-card deck: 22 tarocks + 8 cards in each of 4 suits
Card values: Kings=5, SkÃ¼s/XXI/I=5, Queens=4, Knights=3, Jacks=2, Others=1
Need 36+ points to win positive contract
Call a King to find partner (unless in talon/own hand)

strategy.basic: Focus on collecting high-value cards (kings, honours). In positive contracts, 36 points is the threshold - track your progress toward this goal.
strategy.intermediate: Talon selection is crucial. Evaluate both packets carefully before choosing. When calling a king, consider which suit you need help in.
strategy.advanced: Master the announcement strategy. Announcing bonuses doubles their value but commits you to achieving them. In negative contracts (Bettel, Piccolo), the strategy inverts - you must carefully lose tricks or win exactly the right number.
tips: The SkÃ¼s is the highest trump but can be lost to strategic play - protect it.
In Rufer, watch for the called king to appear - this reveals your partner.
Card counting is essential - track which trumps have been played.
Consider the risk/reward of Sechserdreier carefully - the penalty for losing is significant.
